recent_commits.body:
dq96z_v2: "... collaborators in the projects, not as subjects recruited for a
study." counted as recruiting participants ("subjects recruited"), and the
light was red. New .detect_no_participants(): "no human/animal subjects were
involved/used", "did not involve/include (any) human/animal subjects",
"no animals nor human participants were involved", "not as subjects". It

collections (13,706 papers) it would have changed 18 verdicts, 6 wrongly.

recent_commits.message: data_check warns about keys in a repository; module_run() removes keys from every result (#607)
recent_commits.body:
A PsyArXiv preprint's OSF project (6qf9p_v3) held an OpenRouter key in the
survey flow of two Qualtrics surveys, as embedded data, which the export also
wrote into every response. Metacheck did not warn, and copied the key into its
saved result, which GitHub refused to store.

- R/keys.R: betterleaks' rules of high and medium confidence (427, all
  readable by R with perl = TRUE), with their filters: minimum entropy,
  patterns a key must or must not match, texts, the general placeholders, and
  path conditions. Each rule is tried only near its keywords; keywords are
  found in the unique pieces of a text; encoded data (1,000+ base64
  characters) is masked. Keys are numbered, never returned; only their first
  characters are shown.
- data_check: every downloaded file the authors wrote is searched whole (with
  code_check's downloads, and a local folder's hidden files such as .env); of
  a tabular data file the column names and first 3 rows of the table as read.
  A key turns the light red; the report gives files, lines or rows, type and
  beginning, and how to revoke it; summary column key_n, result table keys.
- module_run(): any key in a module's result is replaced by "[key removed]".
- data-raw/key_patterns.R collects the rules (RcppTOML, its literal strings
  unescaped; checked against Python's tomllib for all 474 rules) into
  inst/databases/key_patterns.Rds; betterleaks' MIT notice in inst/COPYRIGHTS.

Tested with random fake keys of 12 types, on 6qf9p_v3 itself (1 key in 4
files), and on 400 repositories of an earlier corpus run (no find from text
that is not a key, after two fixes the run showed).
Version 0.4.3.17.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.body:

read through the key, but the plain link was reported as "could not check ...
(private)" and counted as a second repository, and prereg_check called the
view-only link an inaccessible registration.

- repo_check: a node read through a view-only link with public = FALSE is a
  private project; the plain link to it is left out. The summary and report
  say "The OSF project ... is private. Metacheck examined the files through
  the view_only link. As the preprint is public, and the OSF Files are
  accessible to anyone, consider making the OSF project public." (the user's
  wording); the light is yellow. New summary column repo_view_only and
  result table view_only.
- osf_type(): the view-only key goes at the end of the address
  (.../guids/<id>/?resolve=false&view_only=<key>); pasted into the middle, the
  OSF did not answer.

Checked live on 8dn4g_v1's links; tests with osf_info() replaced (both links,
the view-only link alone, a public project) and for the address. The three
tests comparing the whole summary table have the new column.
Version 0.4.3.15.

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: file names are escaped before use in a search pattern (#597)
recent_commits.body:
The escape in repro_rewrite_paths() (twice), .repro_upgrade_stan_files() and
.repro_install_error_lines() used a bracket expression that works only with
perl = TRUE, which these gsub() calls left out, so it escaped nothing. A name
with "\P" (a Windows path, 10.1111/2041-210X.13928) or "\6" (jskhb_v1) made an
invalid pattern and stopped the module for the paper; a name with ( [ + or .
was matched loosely. All four now use .repro_sw_escape().

New test with both real cases and names with (1), [1], + and a package name
with a "."; it fails on the old code with the error from the issue.
Version 0.4.3.13.

recent_commits.body:
- New .p_not_test() judges each p-value by the words of its own clause and
  returns "marker", "threshold", "legend" or NA. A p-value that a test
  statistic belongs to is never left out.
- stat_p_exact() leaves these out and keeps the reason in the new table
  column not_a_test. Before, only "*p < .05/.01/.001" was left out, and of a
  note repeated under two tables only one copy.
- Built on 11 collections (5,378 papers) and tested on 6 others (6,543
  papers): 18,377 flagged before, 13,216 now; of 300 random p-values left out
  there, none was an imprecisely reported result.
- Version 0.4.3.10.

recent_commits.message: Code check: a file the code writes is not a missing file; SAS, SPSS and Mplus ignore capitals
recent_commits.body:
code_file_refs() took every file name in Python's open(), MATLAB's fopen()
and Mplus's FILE = as an input, so open("out.txt", "w"), fopen('x.txt', 'w')
and the FILE = of SAVEDATA: were reported as files the repository lacks.
A call whose mode creates the file, and the SAVEDATA command, are now left
out (.code_blank_write_opens(), .code_blank_mplus_savedata());
.py_open_writes() uses the same reading of the mode.

SAS, SPSS and Mplus ignore capitals, but only one way of writing each
command was found: PROC IMPORT DATAFILE= and INFILE in SAS, get file= in
SPSS and file = in Mplus were never checked. The search now ignores
capitals for these languages.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Web address check: urlchecker 2.0.0 no longer stops before the rules apply
recent_commits.body:
urlchecker 2.0.0 stops by itself on a bad address (fail = TRUE), so the
rules for large files and time-outs never ran. fail = FALSE where the
installed version has it. Run here with urlchecker 2.0.0: it tries again,
warns about an address that did not answer, and passes.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Web address check: an address that does not answer on both tries is a warning
recent_commits.body:
GitHub's machines could not connect to CRAN.R-project.org within 5 seconds,
twice in a row and in two runs. A time-out is a network condition, not a
wrong address; every other error still fails the check.

recent_commits.message: Correct four statements in NEWS.md and the docs
recent_commits.body:
* DEBIT's formula argument was not new: it gains "exact", and its three
  values that always failed were removed.
* audit() finds tally columns by the names duplicate_tally() gave them,
  not by type, so a renamed one is left out; ?duplicate_tally says so.
* grim_plot_grid()'s rounding and threshold also apply to mapper output
  that lost the record of its call.
* The Deprecated section lists audit_seq() and audit_total_n().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Break ties between two sums of one remainder exactly in grimmer_closest()
recent_commits.body:
* sums_closest_by_remainder() compared x * n_items as a double, so where
  two sums with the same remainder were equally close, as with
  items_averaged >= 10^digits_x, the noise in the product picked one:
  grimmer_closest(8.3, 0.1, 2, 1, 1, 15, "integer") gave 250, not 248.
  It compares whole numbers now, as the later tie-breaks already did.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Run the tests on at most two cores under R CMD check
recent_commits.body:
* testthat took the number of workers from options(Ncpus) or TESTTHAT_CPUS,
  so a machine that sets either high used more than the two cores CRAN
  allows: the tests took 401 s of CPU in 116 s with four. tests/testthat.R
  sets Ncpus to 2, which testthat reads first; devtools::test() is
  unaffected.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Describe when grim_plot_grid() uses rounding, threshold, and an inferred digits_x
recent_commits.body:
* The docs named data built by hand as the case for its rounding and
  threshold arguments and for inferring digits_x from x, but grim_plot_grid()
  refuses anything other than mapper output, which records its settings and
  has a digits_x column. They now name show_data = FALSE and a removed
  digits_x column instead, and so does NEWS.md.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Refuse grimmer_closest() on too many sums, and break its mean ties exactly
recent_commits.body:
* For a consistent value set, grimmer_closest() checks one sum per remainder
  modulo n against the SD, one at a time: 35 seconds for n = 9e6, where
  grimmer() takes a tenth of one. More than 100,000 such sums is an error
  now, as for grimmer() at a million. It takes an n above about
  10^(digits_x + 5).
* With no mean reported as x, it picked between two equally close sums by the
  noise in the means, so that it could disagree with grim_closest() since
  70a6159 made that one exact. Both compare whole numbers now.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Order alpha after alternative in grim_binomial_power(), and keep a tiny SE
recent_commits.body:
* grim_binomial() and binom.test() take alternative before the significance
  level; grim_binomial_power() took them the other way around. Both are new
  in 1.0.0.
* The sd_binary_*() functions took the root of the product of the variance
  and the denominator ratio, which underflows for an SE at an n of about
  1e300. They take the product of the roots.
* A comment in grim_exp_incon() still said its NA cases are exactly those of
  grim().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Find tally columns by name, and name the class and cause in two errors
recent_commits.body:
* audit() on duplicate_tally() output took any integer column with the
  suffix as a tally column, such as one that mutate() added as extra_n.
  duplicate_tally() now records the names of its tally columns, and audit()
  reads those.
* Grouped duplicate_tally() output got only "See ?audit" since 51ce062.
  It gets the hint that group_by() removed the class again, without calling
  it mapper output.
* explain_print() on a plain data frame named the tibble class it had turned
  it into, not the class it was given.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write a negative zero and a large product the same in every context
recent_commits.body:
* The marker of a line plot labeled a mean of round(-0.001, 2) "-0.00",
  although the axis wrote it as "0.00".
* The 2^53 error wrote its product as 5.2e+16 from grim() but in full from
  grim_explain(), which sets scipen for its text. It is now 5.2e16 in both,
  like the 9.007e15 next to it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep the 0.6.1 names of renamed arguments and functions working, with a warning
recent_commits.body:
* split_by_parens(sep, check_sep), before_parens(sep), inside_parens(sep),
  sd_binary_mean_n(mean), and manage_helper_col(var_arg, affix) failed with
  R's "unused argument" error. They now warn and pass the value on under the
  new name; use_renamed_arg() does this for all but manage_helper_col(),
  which needs the unevaluated argument and so rebuilds its call.
* audit_seq() and audit_total_n() are exported again as deprecated aliases of
  the audit() methods, which now hold their bodies. They still refuse output
  of another tier.
* grim_plot() has its 0.6.1 signature again, so that positional calls reach
  n rather than split_by_digits. Its removed color and alpha arguments are
  ignored with a warning.
* Tests call audit() where they called audit_seq() or audit_total_n().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Call a negative percentage inconsistent with the count and n both missing
recent_commits.body:
* percentage_of() returned NA whenever absolute was missing along with n,
  although no count gives a share below 0. That case is FALSE now, as it
  was with n given.
* The technical-notes vignette said DEBIT with n missing searches only for an
  SE too large for a population SD. It searches for any SE.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Break ties in grim_closest() and grimmer_closest() by a stated rule
recent_commits.body:
* grim_closest() took the tie between two equally close means from round()
  on the sum, which rounds half to even, so 0.5 with n = 17 and n = 19 went
  different ways. It now compares distances as whole numbers and returns
  the smaller mean.
* grimmer_closest() picked between two equally close SDs of one sum by the
  noise in their roots. The smaller SD now wins, with the tolerance the
  comparison across sums already had.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let zoom = "medium" reach a neighbor that a limit leaves room for, or warn
recent_commits.body:
* The search for the nearest attainable values stopped at 9,999 values per
  side, even where a limit cut one side short, so the 0% row of one case
  never reached 100%. It now spends its 20,000 values on the side that has
  room for them.
* Under "medium", a row that still has no neighbor on a side gets a
  warning, as an empty row under "close" did. The docs state the limit.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return a row of NA from grimmer_values() where a missing value forces TRUE
recent_commits.body:
* A missing digits_*, items_averaged, or n can force grimmer() to TRUE, but
  the pairs behind it are still open. grimmer_values() went on to enumerate
  them and crashed; it now checks every value, as grimmer_closest() and
  debit_values() do.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say in debit_values()'s size error that the SD hasn't narrowed the count yet
recent_commits.body:
* It said the value set admits more than a million samples, though it counts
the numbers of ones whose mean would be reported as x, before the SD rules
most of them out, as the docs say.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that sd_meaning must have length 1 in the sd_binary_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* Two values used to give "must be one of ...", naming a valid first value
as the culprit.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Describe the 1.0.0 changes in NEWS.md as 0.6.1 users know the functions
recent_commits.body:
* sd_meaning and grim_grid() are new, so they did not change position or
argument name, and grim_plot_grid()'s raster color was grim_plot()'s.

* audit_seq() and audit_total_n() are no longer exported, so the fixes in
them are described as fixes of audit() on sequence and total-n output.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let grim_plot() take the new argument names, too
recent_commits.body:
* It passed digits_x and color_raster in every call, so a call that already
used these names failed with "matched by multiple actual arguments". The
old names now default to lifecycle::deprecated() and are passed on only if
given.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write the continuous-data line of the missing data_type error as plain text
recent_commits.body:
* cli doesn't interpolate the text it splices into a bullet, so the listing
and plotting functions printed a literal `{name_fn}()`, and the tests
printed a stray backslash where the line was continued.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix a crash and the tie-break of grimmer_closest()
recent_commits.body:
* For n from 2 to 4, a sum whose remainder fails test 3 passed an NA range
to the search for attainable sums of squares, which stopped with "missing
value where TRUE/FALSE needed". Such sums are now dropped first.

* Ties between equally close SDs went by floating-point noise rather than
by the mean closer to x, then the smaller sum: deviations are now computed
so that mirror remainders keep them equal, SDs on either side of sd within
a tolerance count as tied, and the distance to x is counted in units of
its last decimal place.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give the two new sweep tests a fixed seed for CRAN
recent_commits.body:
* sweep_seed() forces its fixed seed, so that a missing one fails under
devtools::test() too, not only in R CMD check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give debit_values() a formula argument
recent_commits.body:
* It mirrors debit()'s signature now, as sd_meaning does. Like
"sd_sample_or_pop" there, "mean_n" is an error: it takes the mean as
anything that would be reported as x, so there is no finite list of
values. "exact" is the default and the only value allowed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show grimmer_closest(), debit_values(), and debit_plot_line() in the vignettes
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add debit_values() and debit_plot_line()
recent_commits.body:
* debit_values() is the counterpart of grim_values() and
grimmer_values() for DEBIT: every number of ones among n binary values
whose mean and SD would be reported as x and sd, with the mean, the SD,
and the number of ones as sum. It lists actual samples, so it follows
formula = "exact", and like grimmer_values() it takes one SD premise per
call. The ones come from the range and spreads that debit_scalar()
decides by, and a brute-force test checks every number of ones by hand.

* debit_plot_line() draws the comb of SDs that debit() admits for one
value set, like grimmer_plot_line(), from 0 to 1 at its widest. It takes
formula, since it only asks debit() about each SD.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add grimmer_closest()
recent_commits.body:
* The counterpart of grim_closest(): the achievable pair whose SD is
closest to sd, among the pairs reported as x and sd if the value set is
consistent, else among those whose mean is reported as x, or has the
mean grim_closest() returns. One row per value set, in the shape of
grimmer_values().

* It lists no pairs: sums with the same remainder modulo n have the same
SDs, so each remainder is tried once, with the sum of squares nearest
the target found directly for n >= 5 (vectorized) and by windowed search
through sum_squares_attainable() for fewer numbers.

* A brute-force test over all samples of 2 to 5 whole numbers checks
the distance to sd under three SD premises.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give manage_helper_col() plain argument names
recent_commits.body: * var_arg is now arg and affix is add_col, which say what they are.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Expect the new settings order in the GRIMMER and DEBIT mapper tests
recent_commits.body:
* f255767 moved sd_meaning ahead of rounding, and the expected settings
tibbles in two tests still listed the old order.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Unexport audit_seq() and audit_total_n()
recent_commits.body:
* audit() dispatches to them on sequence and total-n output and also
supports .by, which they don't, so they were a second, lesser way to do
the same thing. They stay as internal functions behind the audit()
methods.

* ?audit-special now documents the classes of sequence and total-n
output, for writing S3 methods, and the mapper pages and vignettes call
audit().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Call the decimal count digits_x in the grid functions too
recent_commits.body:
* grim_plot_grid() and grim_grid() took it as digits, where every other
function, and the digits_x column they read, says digits_x.
grim_plot_grid()'s raster_color is color_raster, like the color_*
arguments of the line plots. The deprecated grim_plot() still takes
the old names and forwards them.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Call the bracket pair of the parens functions delim
recent_commits.body:
* split_by_parens(), before_parens(), and inside_parens() took the pair
of brackets as sep, which decimal_places() and restore_zeros() use for
the decimal mark. It is delim now, and split_by_parens()'s check_sep is
check_delim. Values are unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

repos.readme_excerpt:
**Text, section, table and statistic extraction from academic papers (PDF, DOCX, HTML), built
for meta-science.**

docpluck turns a research article into text you can run statistical checks on. It extracts the
text layer, repairs the damage extraction itself causes (lost minus signs, split ligatures,
interleaved columns, Greek letters decoded as Latin), identifies the paper's sections, pulls
tables out as cell grids, flattens table rows into records a statistics checker can read, and
renders the whole paper as Markdown. Every output carries a record of what the library had to
guess or refused

recent_commits.message: fix: line-end hyphen and DOI repair, running-title strip, typed descriptive table cells, caption rows out of the grid
recent_commits.body:
Batch of fixes from a two-model check of 10 never-processed psychology papers and
from defects reported by downstream consumers. See CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

Normalization
- extract_pdf runs one pdftotext -bbox pass (restore_line_end_hyphens=True) so
  plain-text callers get the layout-gated hyphen restores; a failed pass is
  recorded as line_end_hyphen_words_unavailable.
- W0v restores a hyphen inside a DOI broken at a line end; W0t handles compounds
  of three or more parts; W0u adjacency fix.
- S6u rejoins a URL or DOI broken across a line; capital-initials and list
  numbers keep the break. A list number is no longer glued onto the previous DOI.
- S0h keeps hyphens in documents whose font encodes the printed hyphen as U+00AD
  (document-level gate).
- P0t strips running titles repeated on later pages, publisher watermark
  sentences and "Downloaded from" stamps; ORCID URLs and supplementary-material
  body lines are kept.

Tables
- fields_raw on every flattened record (printed tokens).
- Typed descriptive pairs (M (SD), b (SE), n (%), est [CI]) with fields["group"]
  per arm column; new keys SE, count, pct.
- Nested spanning headers are not read as arm groups.
- Caption, label and running-head rows leave the grid for the caption; text-only
  tables keep their data rows out of the header.
- A captionless page directly continuing the previous table is linked
  (continuation_of, caption_status "continuation").

Sections and references
- Reference numbers separated from their entries are paired back via layout.
- Group, bare-surname and full-first-name authors start their own entry.
- A wrapped "Supplemental Materials." no longer opens a false section; an
  unheaded abstract of 1200-1500 characters is kept.

Tests: 4309 passed. Snapshot checksums re-pinned for 11 fixtures after verifying
every changed line is a hyphen insertion. 125-paper render diff reviewed: no
statistic lost.

recent_commits.message: Match target studies whose labels carry a title
recent_commits.body:
A real gpt-5.5 run on Yu et al. (2024) labelled studies as
'Study 4: Feeling Gratitude Toward Close Versus Distant Others'; the
trailing-token match found no number, so 'Study 4' resolved to nothing
and isolation fell back to the generative method. The study number is
now taken from 'Study/Experiment N' anywhere in the label first.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Label-based multi-study isolation in production
recent_commits.body:
Isolation now defaults to the label method prototyped in
benchmarks/parser_eval/study_labels.py: one experiment-model call labels
every paragraph and sentence of the paper by study (labels only, no
text), and the target study's text is assembled deterministically from
the paper's own sentences (shared + target units, in order). Text is
verbatim, so nothing is paraphrased or dropped by regeneration; sentences
imported through a cross-reference carry a short
'[From Study X, cited for: <aspect>]' prefix, and the judge prompt now
says the target's own text takes precedence over imported lines.

New backend/services/study_labels.py holds the pure parts: a segmenter
that also handles PDF text layers (hard wraps, no blank lines, heading
lines, tables), the labelling prompt, label validation, target matching
("2" / "Study 2" / "Experiment 2" / single-study papers) and the filter.
On the CLI the labels are cached per paper, so every study of a paper
reuses one labelling call.

extract_experiment_specific_paper_text dispatches by method
(ISOLATION_METHOD, default labels) and falls back to the generative
rewrite when labelling fails; results and Redis record
multi_study_isolation_method and the fallback reason. Multi-study and
supplement runs now build the paper evidence from the original document,
with isolated chunks placed on its pages by word alignment.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: One canonical text per document
recent_commits.body:
The selected parser's output is now the single text the judge, retrieval
and the evidence text pane use. Previously, whenever the evidence viewer
was built (every web run), PDFs were re-chunked from PyMuPDF's text
layer and that text replaced the parser output, so GROBID/DPT2/bibr
results never reached the judge and partially scanned PDFs lost their
OCR. build_pdf_evidence_source now chunks the parser text and places each
chunk on the pages by aligning its words to the PDF word stream
(_DocumentWords: tolerant of running heads, page numbers and page
breaks); unplaceable chunks carry no offsets so the viewer searches
instead. Without parser text the text layer stays canonical.

Corpora built without the evidence viewer (plain CLI, eval scripts,
lazy builds in run_comparison) now use corpus_segments, the same
chunking, display normalisation and reference flags as the evidence
builder, so both paths embed identical segments. PDF registrations get
the same clean_document_text pass as other formats; number-only lines
are dropped only for PDF-derived text (an OSF answer of "300" was being
deleted). Corpus truncation at MAX_EMBEDDING_SEGMENTS is now logged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Judge independent dimensions in parallel
recent_commits.body:
All three orchestrators now dispatch dimensions through one helper,
_judge_dimensions. Without --append-previous-output the dimensions are
independent and run concurrently (DIMENSION_CONCURRENCY, default 4, per
job); partial and final results stay in dimension order. With the append
chain they run strictly in sequence as before.

Corpora are built once before fan-out (_ensure_text_corpora), which also
stops consensus strands from embedding the same documents once per
voter; the lazily-built full-paper corpus is guarded by a lock. Because
parallel threads write relevance scores into the shared evidence
manifest, it is persisted once after the dimensions finish (and per
dimension only in the sequential case).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Worker: oldest-first queue, independent heartbeat, evidence off the loop
recent_commits.body:
Producers now LPUSH and the worker keeps popping the tail (BRPOPLPUSH),
so jobs run first-in-first-out; jobs reclaimed from a dead worker are
RPUSHed to the tail and run next. The heartbeat is refreshed by its own
task every TTL/3 instead of once per dequeue iteration, which stalled
while all job slots were busy and let a peer reclaim (and re-run) live
jobs. The orchestrators' synchronous evidence building and corpus
embedding now run via asyncio.to_thread so they no longer block the
event loop (and with it the heartbeat and other jobs).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Keep supplements out of the references section; fix label-not-found framing
recent_commits.body:
Supplementary material appended after a paper's reference list was
flagged in_references and dropped from retrieval, disabling --supplement.
The references span now ends at the next merged-document separator
(DOCUMENT_SEPARATOR_RE), in both the evidence-builder flags and the
heading fallback in _reference_chunk_ids, and the separator line is a
chunk boundary.

For label_not_found_full_text runs the judge was told the paper reports
several studies and was pre-filtered; it now gets a variant that says the
label is absent, the excerpts are unfiltered, and the paper may report a
single study.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Price gpt-6.1-terra in the cost table
recent_commits.body:
Standard-tier OpenAI pricing for <=272K-token context ($1.00 input,
$5.00 output per 1M tokens), so llm_usd is estimated instead of 0.0.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Surface supplement references; add --supplement to the CLI
recent_commits.body:
Detect references to supplementary material in the paper body
(supplement/supplemental/supplementary, supporting information, online
material[s]; the trailing reference list is ignored) and record
paper_references_supplement plus up to three matched snippets
(paper_supplement_mentions) on the result. When the paper points to a
supplement the run lacks, the judge is told to say so for unlocated
registered elements. The CLI's repeatable --supplement PATH (and a
'supplement' batch-manifest column) appends parsed supplements to the
paper under labelled separators, after isolation so they are never
trimmed; supplying them suppresses the judge note.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Readable JATS tables; isolation retains footnotes and table notes
recent_commits.body:
extract_text_from_xml now emits one line per <tr> with cells joined by
' | ' (block tags inside a cell become spaces), drops layout whitespace
between table elements, and keeps <label>/<caption> before the table
body and table-wrap-foot notes after it. The isolation prompt explicitly
retains footnotes, table notes, captions, table contents and author
notes attached to included content; bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Ask the judge for likely alternatives; guarantee a semantic floor
recent_commits.body:
The unlocated_in_* instructions now ask for synonyms AND the most likely
alternatives a deviating document would state instead (pairwise ->
listwise, Prolific -> MTurk), which the literal scan searches. Term
parsing accepts comma/semicolon/'or' separators, keeps parenthesised
semicolons inside one element, and folds hyphens. _targeted_element_search
returns the top semantic hits even below the threshold when the literal
scan finds nothing, and reserves slots so literal hits are not crowded
out by scored semantic hits.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Targeted verification searches the true full paper
recent_commits.body:
When multi-study isolation trimmed the paper, thread the pre-isolation
text into run_comparison and build a lazily-created, cached FULLPAPER_
corpus used only by _targeted_element_search for paper-side elements,
so footnotes and sections dropped by isolation stay reachable. Hits
already shown to the judge are de-duplicated by text containment;
hits from outside the isolated text are prefixed with
[outside the isolated target-study text] and the block explains how to
weigh them. Registration-side searches and reference-chunk exclusion are
unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Isolation quality gate with full-text fallback and label pre-check
recent_commits.body:
Reject refusal-shaped or near-empty isolation output (shorter than
max(2000 chars, 5% of the paper), capped at half the source), never cache
it, and fall back to the full paper with multi_study_isolation=
"fallback_full_text". Skip isolation entirely when the study label (or a
Study/Experiment variant) never occurs in the paper
("label_not_found_full_text"). Multi-pass ensembles drop refused drafts
before the union. The isolation status is mirrored onto ComparisonResult
and the CLI batch summary so Redis-less runs can detect it; the report
banner covers the new statuses. Bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.

repos.readme_excerpt:
OIF (Output It Forward) is a Chrome extension that helps researchers detect and document open data indicators in scholarly articles while they browse. As you read a paper, OIF automatically scans the page for phrases and repository links commonly associated with open data practices, and logs matches to a running CSV file for systematic documentation.
OIF is designed with adaptability in mind: its phrase list and repository domain list are plain, editable text files, so tailoring the extension to your discipline requires no programming expertise, just edit a list.

highlights.body:
A PsyArXiv preprint's OSF project (6qf9p_v3) held an OpenRouter key in the
survey flow of two Qualtrics surveys, as embedded data, which the export also
wrote into every response. Metacheck did not warn, and copied the key into its
saved result, which GitHub refused to store.

- R/keys.R: betterleaks' rules of high and medium confidence (427, all
  readable by R with perl = TRUE), with their filters: minimum entropy,
  patterns a key must or must not match, texts, the general placeholders, and
  path conditions. Each rule is tried only near its keywords; keywords are
  found in the unique pieces of a text; encoded data (1,000+ base64
  characters) is masked. Keys are numbered, never returned; only their first
  characters are shown.
- data_check: every downloaded file the authors wrote is searched whole (with
  code_check's downloads, and a local folder's hidden files such as .env); of
  a tabular data file the column names and first 3 rows of the table as read.
  A key turns the light red; the report gives files, lines or rows, type and
  beginning, and how to revoke it; summary column key_n, result table keys.
- module_run(): any key in a module's result is replaced by "[key removed]".
- data-raw/key_patterns.R collects the rules (RcppTOML, its literal strings
  unescaped; checked against Python's tomllib for all 474 rules) into
  inst/databases/key_patterns.Rds; betterleaks' MIT notice in inst/COPYRIGHTS.

Tested with random fake keys of 12 types, on 6qf9p_v3 itself (1 key in 4
files), and on 400 repositories of an earlier corpus run (no find from text
that is not a key, after two fixes the run showed).

highlights.message: Refuse an old argument name given along with its new one
highlights.body:
* The shims of renamed arguments used the old name's value and dropped
  the new one without a word, as in split_by_parens(sep = "brackets",
  delim = "braces"). Giving both is an error now, in manage_helper_col()
  too.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Correct four statements in NEWS.md and the docs
highlights.body:
* DEBIT's formula argument was not new: it gains "exact", and its three
  values that always failed were removed.
* audit() finds tally columns by the names duplicate_tally() gave them,
  not by type, so a renamed one is left out; ?duplicate_tally says so.
* grim_plot_grid()'s rounding and threshold also apply to mapper output
  that lost the record of its call.
* The Deprecated section lists audit_seq() and audit_total_n().
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Break ties between two sums of one remainder exactly in grimmer_closest()
highlights.body:
* sums_closest_by_remainder() compared x * n_items as a double, so where
  two sums with the same remainder were equally close, as with
  items_averaged >= 10^digits_x, the noise in the product picked one:
  grimmer_closest(8.3, 0.1, 2, 1, 1, 15, "integer") gave 250, not 248.
  It compares whole numbers now, as the later tie-breaks already did.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Run the tests on at most two cores under R CMD check
highlights.body:
* testthat took the number of workers from options(Ncpus) or TESTTHAT_CPUS,
  so a machine that sets either high used more than the two cores CRAN
  allows: the tests took 401 s of CPU in 116 s with four. tests/testthat.R
  sets Ncpus to 2, which testthat reads first; devtools::test() is
  unaffected.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Describe when grim_plot_grid() uses rounding, threshold, and an inferred digits_x
highlights.body:
* The docs named data built by hand as the case for its rounding and
  threshold arguments and for inferring digits_x from x, but grim_plot_grid()
  refuses anything other than mapper output, which records its settings and
  has a digits_x column. They now name show_data = FALSE and a removed
  digits_x column instead, and so does NEWS.md.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Refuse grimmer_closest() on too many sums, and break its mean ties exactly
highlights.body:
* For a consistent value set, grimmer_closest() checks one sum per remainder
  modulo n against the SD, one at a time: 35 seconds for n = 9e6, where
  grimmer() takes a tenth of one. More than 100,000 such sums is an error
  now, as for grimmer() at a million. It takes an n above about
  10^(digits_x + 5).
* With no mean reported as x, it picked between two equally close sums by the
  noise in the means, so that it could disagree with grim_closest() since
  70a6159 made that one exact. Both compare whole numbers now.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Order alpha after alternative in grim_binomial_power(), and keep a tiny SE
highlights.body:
* grim_binomial() and binom.test() take alternative before the significance
  level; grim_binomial_power() took them the other way around. Both are new
  in 1.0.0.
* The sd_binary_*() functions took the root of the product of the variance
  and the denominator ratio, which underflows for an SE at an n of about
  1e300. They take the product of the roots.
* A comment in grim_exp_incon() still said its NA cases are exactly those of
  grim().
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Find tally columns by name, and name the class and cause in two errors
highlights.body:
* audit() on duplicate_tally() output took any integer column with the
  suffix as a tally column, such as one that mutate() added as extra_n.
  duplicate_tally() now records the names of its tally columns, and audit()
  reads those.
* Grouped duplicate_tally() output got only "See ?audit" since 51ce062.
  It gets the hint that group_by() removed the class again, without calling
  it mapper output.
* explain_print() on a plain data frame named the tibble class it had turned
  it into, not the class it was given.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Write a negative zero and a large product the same in every context
highlights.body:
* The marker of a line plot labeled a mean of round(-0.001, 2) "-0.00",
  although the axis wrote it as "0.00".
* The 2^53 error wrote its product as 5.2e+16 from grim() but in full from
  grim_explain(), which sets scipen for its text. It is now 5.2e16 in both,
  like the 9.007e15 next to it.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Keep the 0.6.1 names of renamed arguments and functions working, with a warning
highlights.body:
* split_by_parens(sep, check_sep), before_parens(sep), inside_parens(sep),
  sd_binary_mean_n(mean), and manage_helper_col(var_arg, affix) failed with
  R's "unused argument" error. They now warn and pass the value on under the
  new name; use_renamed_arg() does this for all but manage_helper_col(),
  which needs the unevaluated argument and so rebuilds its call.
* audit_seq() and audit_total_n() are exported again as deprecated aliases of
  the audit() methods, which now hold their bodies. They still refuse output
  of another tier.
* grim_plot() has its 0.6.1 signature again, so that positional calls reach
  n rather than split_by_digits. Its removed color and alpha arguments are
  ignored with a warning.
* Tests call audit() where they called audit_seq() or audit_total_n().
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Call a negative percentage inconsistent with the count and n both missing
highlights.body:
* percentage_of() returned NA whenever absolute was missing along with n,
  although no count gives a share below 0. That case is FALSE now, as it
  was with n given.
* The technical-notes vignette said DEBIT with n missing searches only for an
  SE too large for a population SD. It searches for any SE.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Break ties in grim_closest() and grimmer_closest() by a stated rule
highlights.body:
* grim_closest() took the tie between two equally close means from round()
  on the sum, which rounds half to even, so 0.5 with n = 17 and n = 19 went
  different ways. It now compares distances as whole numbers and returns
  the smaller mean.
* grimmer_closest() picked between two equally close SDs of one sum by the
  noise in their roots. The smaller SD now wins, with the tolerance the
  comparison across sums already had.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Let zoom = "medium" reach a neighbor that a limit leaves room for, or warn
highlights.body:
* The search for the nearest attainable values stopped at 9,999 values per
  side, even where a limit cut one side short, so the 0% row of one case
  never reached 100%. It now spends its 20,000 values on the side that has
  room for them.
* Under "medium", a row that still has no neighbor on a side gets a
  warning, as an empty row under "close" did. The docs state the limit.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Return a row of NA from grimmer_values() where a missing value forces TRUE
highlights.body:
* A missing digits_*, items_averaged, or n can force grimmer() to TRUE, but
  the pairs behind it are still open. grimmer_values() went on to enumerate
  them and crashed; it now checks every value, as grimmer_closest() and
  debit_values() do.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Say in debit_values()'s size error that the SD hasn't narrowed the count yet
highlights.body:
* It said the value set admits more than a million samples, though it counts
the numbers of ones whose mean would be reported as x, before the SD rules
most of them out, as the docs say.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Say that sd_meaning must have length 1 in the sd_binary_*() functions
highlights.body:
* Two values used to give "must be one of ...", naming a valid first value
as the culprit.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Describe the 1.0.0 changes in NEWS.md as 0.6.1 users know the functions
highlights.body:
* sd_meaning and grim_grid() are new, so they did not change position or
argument name, and grim_plot_grid()'s raster color was grim_plot()'s.

* audit_seq() and audit_total_n() are no longer exported, so the fixes in
them are described as fixes of audit() on sequence and total-n output.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Let grim_plot() take the new argument names, too
highlights.body:
* It passed digits_x and color_raster in every call, so a call that already
used these names failed with "matched by multiple actual arguments". The
old names now default to lifecycle::deprecated() and are passed on only if
given.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Write the continuous-data line of the missing data_type error as plain text
highlights.body:
* cli doesn't interpolate the text it splices into a bullet, so the listing
and plotting functions printed a literal `{name_fn}()`, and the tests
printed a stray backslash where the line was continued.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Fix a crash and the tie-break of grimmer_closest()
highlights.body:
* For n from 2 to 4, a sum whose remainder fails test 3 passed an NA range
to the search for attainable sums of squares, which stopped with "missing
value where TRUE/FALSE needed". Such sums are now dropped first.

* Ties between equally close SDs went by floating-point noise rather than
by the mean closer to x, then the smaller sum: deviations are now computed
so that mirror remainders keep them equal, SDs on either side of sd within
a tolerance count as tied, and the distance to x is counted in units of
its last decimal place.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung
